description: Consent to Participate in a Research Study Pacific Lutheran University Title of Study: The effect of mind wandering and text difficulty on reading comprehension: A replication study. Investigators: Alexis Herion and Cammy Widman, senior undergraduate students Introduction You are being asked to be in a research study conducted at Pacific Lutheran University in Psychology. You were selected to participate because you are at least 18 years old AND: You are a PLU student with a SONA-systems account OR You were recruited via social media The purpose of the study is to see the effect mind wandering and text difficulty has on reading comprehension. The purpose of this is to try to see the level of cognitive difficulty that results in more mind wandering. Also, to see if interest level affects mind wandering and reading comprehension. Description of the Study Procedures If you agree to be in this study, you will be asked to do the following things: Take a reading comprehension test on a computer or smartphone, which consists of eight passages for you to read and answer the corresponding questions at the end of each passage. As you read, you will be interrupted periodically with a question that asks if you were mind wandering while you read the previous sentence. After you finish reading all the passages and answering the corresponding reading comprehension questions, you will rate how interested you were in each passage that you previously read. The test should take you about 15 to 30 minutes. Some sample questions we will ask are: â€œThe purpose of this passage is toâ€ and â€œThe best title for this selection would beâ€ with responses in a multiple-choice format. The questions asked will be regarding the reading passages, such as the purpose of the passage, details about the textâ€™s key events or characters and your overall interest in each passage. There will be no questions that could link your identity to your responses on the test. Risks/Benefits/Compensation There are no anticipated significant risks, benefits, or compensation for completing this study. Anonymity Your responses will be strictly anonymous; we will not be collecting or retaining any information about your identity. The findings will be presented at the 2020 Western Psychological Association Convention in San Francisco. The SPSS and Excel files of the participantsâ€™ anonymous data will be archived indefinitely on the researchersâ€™ password protected laptops and will be uploaded onto the projectâ€™s Open Science Framework (OSF) page. OSF is a website dedicated to promoting research and facilitating collaboration. Right to Refuse or Withdraw The decision to participate in this study is entirely up to you. You may refuse to take part in the study at any time without affecting your relationship with the investigators of this study or Pacific Lutheran University. Your decision to refuse will not result in any loss of benefits to which you are otherwise entitled. You have the right not to answer any single question, as well as to withdraw completely from the study at any point during the process. Because your participation is anonymous, it will not be possible to withdraw your survey answers from the study after you have submitted the survey. Right to Ask Questions and Report Concerns You have the right to ask questions about this research and to have those questions answered by the researchers, before, during, or after the study. You may contact the primary investigators, Alexis Herion, at herionaw@plu.edu, and Cammy Widman, at widmancm@plu.edu, or the primary investigatorsâ€™ faculty advisor Heidi McLaughlin at mclaughlinh@plu.edu. If you have any other concerns about your rights as a research participant, you may contact the Human Participants Review Board, Pacific Lutheran University through the Provostâ€™s Office at (253) 535-7126. Consent By clicking below to be taken to the survey, you indicate that you have read and understood the above, that you are at least 18 years of age, that you willingly agree to participate, and that you are not waiving any legal claims. If you would like to keep a copy of this document for your records, please save this page now.
